=== Testimony Docket N0.59475.docx ===
Testimony - PUC Docket No. 59475
Ref: Tracts: #2647.1; #2647; #2648.
Links: F41
Johnnie F & Alicia M Nemec
177 Watt Road 
Cooperstown, NY 13326

We are the joint owners of property affected by the proposed transmission line project – Link 41- Bell County East – Big Hill 765kV and are proceeding pro se in this matter.
Our property parcel numbers are: #2647; #2647.1; #2648.  The proposed line cuts directly across parcel #2647 and #2648, and is within approximately 500 feet of the existing dwelling located on #2647.1 and now currently rented.  The proposed siting of this line dramatically impacts on the part of our land that is the sole egress and ingress points of our property, making it impossible to sever the area affected from the rest of our property.  
Additionally, our land contains one of the highest elevations in Williamson County and consists of rolling hills that provide lovely views of the surrounding countryside.  Willis Creek crosses our property.  Hence, a key component of its economic value is the aesthetic of these scenic views as well as this water feature.  The proposed line crosses Willis Creek and substantially impacts on the views from every point on our property.  Thus, this project will have a catastrophic impact on this valuable aspect of our land, its priceless visual beauty.  It fundamentally destroys the reasonable enjoyment of our land and its economic value.    
Given the reasonable and expected concerns of potential occupants as to the actual or possible health and environmental impacts, the prospects of continuing rental of our house would be severely limited.  Assuming that we could even find a renter for this dwelling, at best it would command a significantly diminished rent.   The prospect of relocating the dwelling or constructing another one would be both cost prohibitive and economically unviable because the impact on aesthetics and the need to maintain the same entry and exit points would still remain.  This area has experienced rapid growth, escalating land values, and high interest by land investment groups – who are not interested in land with these transmission lines.  Certainly, there is no prospect of selling this land at current market value if these lines are constructed or at this point, even under consideration.  Thus, it severely limits – if not, completely destroys the prospect of future residential or commercial development. 
In addition to the obvious and substantial economic impact, we have deep concerns as to the health and environmental impact including the impact on wildlife and habitat both in the construction and operation of these lines.   Further, we are concerned about the noise pollution originating from these lines and the associated health impacts. 
In summary, this project will make the totality of our land undesirable and effectively unsellable, unrentable, and unlivable.  

Alicia M. Nemec                          Johnnie F. Nemec                 Date: May 25, 2026
